newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades weaken in both sweet, sour deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades weaken in both sweet, sour deals.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices deflated in both the sweet and sour markets Monday, finding pressure from continued fundamental oversupply.

Traders said the latest deals for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James put the grade at only a 15 cents premium to the April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, down 5 cts from Friday and more than 25-30 cts from last Monday.
April WTI stood 25 cts lower at $20.00-10 a barrel.
West Texas Sour/Midland was last done at a $2.65 discount to the WTI/Cushing, about 20 cts lower than the late talk on Friday. Offerings were depressed on abundant supplies.
Traders took note of a virtual laundry list of exporting territories as shipping sours to the U.S. Gulf.
Crude from Mexico, Venezuela, California, Canada and the Gulf of Mexico's new deep-water fields have been joined by Iraqi offerings to move the WTS down to lows established for March barrels.
Other talk on Monday saw April Postings Plus sell last at $2.00, working off a roll of around 22-25 cts for Apr/May WTI.
Midland/WTI talked quietly at a 38-40 discount to the WTI/Cushing, with the Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire market talked 10 cts weaker at 20-30 cts under the WTI/Cushing.
